title: Relax the years beyond the window

blocks.text: A water utility rolls its pipe-renewal plan forward year by year. Its planners use a variant of the lesson's rolling horizon called **relax-and-fix**: in each window, the starts in the window's years are yes/no, and the starts in every *later* year are kept in the model as continuous variables between 0 and 1, instead of being held at 0. The later years are then a cheap look ahead: the window sees roughly what its choices leave for later. As before, the first `keep` years of each window are kept, starts decided in earlier windows are fixed, and the last window keeps everything.

The years are the calendar years of `budgets`, in order, and every start year a project offers is one of them. A window is `window` consecutive years of that list, and its decisions are the starts *in* those years: a start is yes/no when its year is in the window or earlier, and relaxed when it is later. The first window begins at the first year, and each next one begins `keep` years later. The last window is the first one that reaches the final year of `budgets` (or would run past it, in which case it is cut short at that year); it keeps every start it has not yet fixed, and the plan ends there. With 2027 to 2029, `window=2` and `keep=1`, the first window 2027-2028 keeps 2027, and the second, 2028-2029, is the last and keeps 2028 and 2029.

`build(projects, budgets)` gives the whole plan model (at most one start per project, a budget row per year counting each project's spend in every year of work). Write first which variables a window fixes, which it makes integer and which continuous, and what it keeps. Then write `relax_and_fix(projects, budgets, window, keep)` and return the plan, a dict from project name to start year. `projects[n]` holds `"value"` (start year to value) and `"cost"` (spend by year of work). A MathOpt variable becomes continuous with `var.integer = False`.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from relax_fix import relax_and_fix

projects = {
    "tunnel": {"value": {2030: 11}, "cost": [8, 8]},
    "hydrants": {"value": {2030: 9}, "cost": [8]},
    "tower": {"value": {2031: 14, 2032: 10}, "cost": [8]},
    "kiosk": {"value": {2032: 4}, "cost": [3]},
}
budgets = {2030: 8, 2031: 8, 2032: 8}

print("window 1, keep 1:", relax_and_fix(projects, budgets, 1, 1))
print("window 2, keep 1:", relax_and_fix(projects, budgets, 2, 1))
print("window 3, keep 3:", relax_and_fix(projects, budgets, 3, 3))

cases.says: a window as long as the plan solves the whole plan at once
later years are relaxed, not held at zero, so the first window sees what its choice costs them
the window's own years are integer, so a kept plan never splits a project to fit a budget

origin.section: A Rolling Horizon Plans a Few Years at a Time and Keeps Only the First Ones

concepts: a window decides its years with later starts handled apart, keeps its first years and rolls on
